 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 11-01-2020 at about 12.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding towards Kolar town from Malur town in a car bearing No.KA-53-N-7269, driven by her son Harish.

When they reached near Hungenahalli Gate, on Malur-Kolar road, Malur Taluk,
Kolar District, the driver Harish driven the car with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the road side tree.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Doddashivara, wherein she took first aid treatment and thereafter, she was shifted to R. L. Jalappa Hospital, Kolar.
Again she was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took further treatment as an indoor patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was working as tailor and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she became permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Malur Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their counsels.
The respondent No.1 did not choose to file written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing No. KA-53-N-7269 in favour of respondent No.1 and its validity as on the date of accident.

Further it has contended that,
there is unreasonable delay of three days in filing the complaint/FIR and filing of the complaint against the insured vehicle car is an after thought story.
It has contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M. V. Act.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by the petitioner.

2 further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence to drove the same.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 11-01-2020, at about 12.30 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-53-N-7269?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got herself examined as PW-1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Further, she has got examined two more witnesses namely Dr. S. A.
Somashekara and N. Vedhavathi as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and closed her side.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 11-01-2020 at about 12.30 p.m., near Hungenahalli Gate, on Malur-Kolar road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, when she was proceeding in a car bearing No.KA-53-N-7269, the driver of the said car driven the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, she was doing tailoring work and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has became permanently disabled and has lost her earning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., and first information statement, Ex.P.2 is true copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.4 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.5 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.6 is true copy of discharge summary, Ex.P.7 is Varalakshmi vs Vishwa Balaji.A on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133281893/

3 notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.8 is OPD record, Ex.P.9 is X-ray, Ex.P.10 is authorization letter,
Ex.P.11 is copy of In-patient bill and Ex.P.12 are In-patient records.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 5, prima-facia it reveals that, on 11-01- 2020 at about 12.30 p.m., near Hungenahalli Gate, on Malur-Kolar road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, the petitioner was proceeding in a car bearing No. KA-53-N-7269 and the driver of the said car drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree. Due to said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-53-N-7269 the said accident took place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
12. The petitioner, who is examined as P.W.1, has reiterated entire petition averments.
The said facts have remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1, as he did not choose to contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, though the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement and in the cross-examination of P.W.1., it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No. KA-53-N-7269.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

13. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.6 discharge summary,
Ex.P.8 OPD record, Ex.P.11 x-ray and Ex.P.12 IP records, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered fracture of dislocation of left hip.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined and assessed physical disability of the petitioner, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner was diagnosed to have fracture of dislocation of left hip and she has undergone surgery in the form of uncemented total hip replacement on 16-01-2020.
Further, he has deposed that, recent X-ray shows left side THR with components in situ and she has suffered total disability of 41% to her left lower limb and 21% to the whole body.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestion made in his cross-examination that, the implants are causing restrictions to the movements of the petitioner and she will be having no disability on removal of implants.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement or to rebut the oral and documentary evidence led by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-53-N-7269 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.3, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.5, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-N-7269.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of driver of offending car.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: 17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 11-01-2020 at about 12.30 p.m., near Hungenahalli Gate, on Malur- Kolar road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-53- N-7269.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-53- N-7269 and she has sustained closed posterior dislocation of left hip,
fracture head of left femur and left acetabular fracture and for the said injuries she has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc., The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

5 i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.7.
As per Ex.P.7, the date of birth of the petitioner is 10- 05-1965.
The accident has taken place on 11-01-2020 at about 12.30 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 55 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined and assessed physical disability of the petitioner, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner was diagnosed to have fracture of dislocation of left hip and she has undergone surgery in the form of uncemented total hip replacement on 16-01-2020.
Further, he has deposed that, recent X-ray shows left side THR with components in situ and she has suffered total disability of 41% to her left lower limb and 21% to the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.6 discharge summary,
Ex.P.8 OPD record, Ex.P.11 X-ray and Ex.P.12 in-patient records clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered closed posterior dislocation of left hip, fracture head of left femur and left acetabular fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e., uncemented total hip replacement.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length

,
nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made in to him that, the Ex.P.8 and 9 documents are not related to the petitioner, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 11-01-2020 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 13-10-2023, which is after lapse of three and half year from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, he has clearly admitted in his cross- examination that, at the time of assessing the disability there was implants in the body of petitioner and weight of the body will be bear by the implants when it is in the body.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, the P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, there may be some wear and tear due to the age of the petitioner and also admits that he has not mentioned the guidelines based for assessing the disability.

Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12%
to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12%
to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was doing tailoring work and was earning income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do tailoring work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.

She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was Varalakshmi vs Vishwa Balaji.A on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133281893/
6 doing agriculture and milk vending.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2020.

Hence,
the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,74,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 55 years is 11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,74,000 X 12/100 X 11 = Rs.2,29,680/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc.
Further she has stated that, out of total medical expenses, she has paid Rs.79,280/- and an amount of Rs.1,13,589/- has been paid by the Government under Arogya Bhagya Yojane.

In order to prove the same, she has examined Senior Technician in MRD Department of Manipal Hospital as P.W.3 and she has produced in-patient bill,
which is marked Ex.P.11.

The Ex.P.11 in-patient bill has been examined carefully and found that, out of total medical expenses of Rs.1,92,869/-, the petitioner has paid an amount of Rs.79,280/- and Rs.1,13,589/- has been paid by the Government under Arogya Bhagya Yojana.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.79,280/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on her left leg i.e. closed posterior dislocation of left hip, fracture head of left femur and left acetabular fracture.
As per Ex.P.6 discharge summary and Ex.P12 inpatient records, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 07 days from 14-01-2020 to 20-01-2020, in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
She has also underwent surgery i.e. uncemented left total hip replacement.
Further as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.
Therefore, taking into considering the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

iv) Attendant charges: As per Ex.P.6 discharge summary and Ex.P.12 inpatient records, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 07 days from 14-01-2020 to 20-01-2020, in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 7 = Rs.7,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.6 discharge summary and Ex.P.12 inpatient records, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 07 days from 14-01-2020 to 20-01-2020, in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 7 = Rs.5,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Noor Nagar, Kolar, the accident has taken place near Hungenahalli Gate, on Malur-Kolar Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District and she has taken treatment at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.

Taking into consideration the distance in between all the Varalakshmi vs Vishwa Balaji.A on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133281893/
7 above three places, compensation of Rs.6,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days as in-patient at Manipal Hospital for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost her income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.14,500 x 2 = Rs.29,000/-
is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 55 years and unfortunately she has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones i.e. her left leg.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:

The P.W.2 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, at the time of assessing the disability there was implants in the body of petitioner and weight of the body will be bear by the implants when it is in the body.
This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.

Though nothing has been stated by the petitioner or the doctor with regard to removal of implants and cost of surgery for removal of implants, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,29,680-00 2.
Medical expenses 79,280-00 3. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 7,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 5,600-00
6. Conveyance expenses 6,000-00 7. Loss of income during 29,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 4,46,560-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 4,46,560/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

8 20.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-N-7269 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 4,46,560/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,46,560/- (Rupees four lakh forty six thousand five hundred and sixty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 11-01-2020 at about 12.30 p.m., near Hungenahalli Gate, on Malur- Kolar road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-53- N-7269.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.3, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.5, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-N-7269.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of driver of offending car.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, the P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, there may be some wear and tear due to the age of the petitioner and also admits that he has not mentioned the guidelines based for assessing the disability.
Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12%
to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12%
to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was Varalakshmi vs Vishwa Balaji.A on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133281893/
6 doing agriculture and milk vending.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2020.
Hence,
the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,74,000/-.
b)
As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 55 years is 11.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
The P.W.2 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, at the time of assessing the disability there was implants in the body of petitioner and weight of the body will be bear by the implants when it is in the body.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,29,680-00 2.
Medical expenses 79,280-00 3. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 7,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 5,600-00
6. Conveyance expenses 6,000-00 7. Loss of income during 29,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 4,46,560-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 4,46,560/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 4,46,560/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,46,560/- (Rupees four lakh forty six thousand five hundred and sixty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
